rules.title: Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not terminate a tenancy without just cause. At-fault causes include nonpayment, failure to cure a lease violation, nuisance or damage, illegal use, failure to renew a similar agreement, failure to give reasonable access, and an unapproved subtenant. No-fault causes include owner or family move-in, resident manager occupancy, demolition and permanent removal from the rental market, government order, and conversion to affordable housing. No-fault evictions require relocation assistance and a Landlord Declaration of Intent to Evict filed with LAHD. A tenant evicted for an at-fault reason gets no relocation assistance.
rules.key_value: 30-day and 60-day written notice for no-fault evictions (some require 120 days or up to a 1-year extension); relocation assistance and a Declaration of Intent to Evict filed with LAHD required for no-fault evictions; copy of the termination notice filed with LAHD within 3 business days of service

coverage.summary: Covers most residential property in the City of Los Angeles that is not regulated by the RSO. The tenant must have lived in the unit at least six months or the original lease must have expired, whichever comes first. It can apply to buildings newer than October 1, 1978 and to a property with a single single-family dwelling.
coverage.other_conditions: Applies to tenancies where the tenant has lived in the unit at least six months or the original lease has expired, whichever comes first.

rules.exemptions: Transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity or sorority houses, owner's roommate, certain cooperatives, some non-profit homeless or substance-abuse treatment facilities, some HACLA or government-owned properties.
citation_aliases: L.A. Mun. Code ch. XVI, art. 5
rules.quoted_span: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.

rules.title: RSO eviction controls: no-fault eviction relocation, Declaration of Intent to Evict, and notice filing
rules.requirement: For units under the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (and the JCO), every no-fault eviction requires payment of relocation assistance and a Declaration of Intent to Evict filed with LAHD before the tenant is evicted. A termination notice may be served only after the Declaration is filed, and a copy of the notice must be filed with LAHD after service. Failing to file the Declaration makes the eviction a violation. No-fault reasons include owner or relative move-in, resident manager occupancy (allowed only if required by law, an affordable housing covenant, or a regulatory agreement), demolition and removal from the rental market, government order, and conversion to affordable housing.
rules.key_value: Declaration of Intent to Evict filed with LAHD before service of notice; copy of notice filed with LAHD within 3 business days of service (bulletin text elsewhere says 3 days); 30-day and 60-day written notice (some 120 days or up to a 1-year extension); Owner, Eligible Relative, or Resident Manager Occupancy filing fee $75

coverage.summary: Applies to rental units subject to the City's Rent Stabilization Ordinance.
